what_its_for: Topotecan is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of cancer, including ovarian cancer, small cell lung cancer, and cervical cancer. It works by slowing or stopping the growth of cancer cells in your body.
how_to_take: Topotecan comes in two forms: a capsule you swallow by mouth, or an injection given into your vein (IV) by a healthcare provider at a clinic or hospital. If you are taking the capsules, swallow them whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or open the capsules. You can take them with or without food. Try to take your capsules at the same time each day. Handle the capsules carefully — if a capsule breaks open, avoid touching the powder inside. Wash your hands thoroughly after handling.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, height, kidney function, and the type of cancer being treated. The capsule dose is usually taken once a day for 5 days in a row, followed by a rest period, repeating every 21 days. Your doctor may adjust your dose or schedule depending on how your body responds and any side effects you experience. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, do NOT take an extra dose or double up to make up for the missed one. Simply skip the missed dose and take your next scheduled dose at the usual time. If you vomit after taking a dose and can see the capsule in the vomit, do not take another dose — contact your doctor or nurse for guidance. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store topotecan capsules in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep the capsules in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep them away from light and moisture. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do NOT dispose of unused or expired capsules in the trash or toilet — ask your pharmacist about a proper medication take-back program or a special disposal method, since topotecan is a hazardous chemotherapy drug.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who are sick or have infections, since topotecan lowers your immune system and makes it easier for you to get sick. Avoid getting live vaccines (such as flu nasal spray or shingles vaccine) while taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child during treatment, as topotecan can harm an unborn baby — use reliable birth control. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Tell your doctor before taking any new over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as some can interact with topotecan.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following: fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, chills, or signs of infection (since this may mean your infection-fighting white blood cells are dangerously low); unusual or severe bruising or bleeding; extreme tiredness or weakness; shortness of breath or chest pain; severe diarrhea or stomach pain; blood in your urine, stool, or vomit; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; or if you feel faint or dizzy. Also call your doctor if you notice your skin or eyes turning yellow, or if you have severe mouth sores.
when_it_works: Topotecan starts working right away to fight cancer cells, but you may not feel or see the effects immediately. It often takes several treatment cycles (weeks to months) before your doctor can measure how well the treatment is working. Your doctor will schedule regular blood tests and scans to monitor your progress. Do not be discouraged if you do not notice changes right away — keep taking the medicine as directed and attend all your follow-up appointments.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. If your kidneys are not working well, your dose may need to be lowered. Liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially low blood counts, and will be monitored closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Topotecan can seriously harm an unborn baby and should NOT be used during pregnancy. Women of childbearing age must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose. Men should use contraception for at least 3 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Children: The safety and effectiveness in children have not been fully established for all uses — your doctor will guide you if this medicine is being used for a child.
